A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniEgoMotion study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, forecasting and generation experiments on EE4D-Motion, including quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and ablations, with limited revisions to the reported EgoAllo comparison.

M1.justification: The diffusion model, image conditioning, masking, forecasting procedure and head-centric motion representation are unchanged. The relocated representation appendix and new Figure 7 explain the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three egocentric tasks on EE4D-Motion. The clarified distinction between 208 processed hours and 110 retained hours does not establish expanded training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains AvatarPoser, EgoEgo and EgoAllo; Table 2 retains LSTM and Two-stage. No comparator is added or removed, and the added head/device-transform description does not establish a changed baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: Appendix B extends the exclusion from head-rotation and head-translation evaluation to EgoAllo, reflected in Table 1. The splits, 143K training samples, 4400 validation samples, clip lengths and forecasting horizon remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 3 and 6 revise the EgoAllo reconstruction examples and vertex-error maps, changing the qualitative evidence about reconstruction failures. The architecture, representation, encoder and conditioning-input ablations in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The practice of reporting single metric values is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces EgoAllo's head-rotation error of 0.531 and head-translation error of 0.130 with dashes. Its depicted poses and error colors change in Figures 3 and 6. All other numerical entries in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulations, diffusion equations, motion canonicalization and SMPL-X fitting objective are unchanged. Figure 7 illustrates an existing decomposition without introducing new mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified three-task model, image-based scene conditioning, EE4D-Motion and state-of-the-art reconstruction performance.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes the explanation linking EgoAllo's head-tracking errors to a pelvis-centric representation. It instead emphasizes floor-grounding problems associated with its kinematic chain and local joint angles. Appendix B explains the exclusion of its head-tracking metrics.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies EgoAllo's fixed head/device transformation. Appendix G distinguishes 208 processed hours from 110 hours retained after filtering, whereas v1 describes 110+ hours without that accounting. Training hyperparameters, hardware and project access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 102 cited works and Related Work section are unchanged. Section 4.3 makes a limited correction to the comparison with EgoAllo by dropping its pelvis-centric characterization, consistent with the head-centric description already present in Appendix B.

P1.justification: Motion Representation moves from supplementary Section F to D, shifting the text-conditioning and training sections to E and F. Local paragraph edits and a supplementary-material pointer leave the broader narrative unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 illustrating motion canonicalization, replaces the EgoAllo panels in Figures 3 and 6, and reflows the appendix. The existing table structures and other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The explained removal of EgoAllo's head-tracking scores and revised interpretation reduce inconsistencies in the comparison (Table 1, Section 4.3 and Appendix B). Clearer data-filtering totals and Figure 7 improve transparency and understanding. These are limited reporting improvements; the reason for replacing the EgoAllo qualitative outputs remains unspecified.
